text:
maya: Heads up — ran into a weird rotation edge in the sampleapp during demo prep. After rotating the project-scoped API key we still saw some 401s for about 30s. Pretty sure it's the SDK keeping the old key in an in-memory credential cache used by the long-lived streamer.

sam: Ugh. Is the stream reusing a cached Authorization header? We recently added a small LRU cache for credentials to avoid KMS calls.

maya: Yeah looks like that. Repro steps: 1) sampleapp uses REDWOOD_API_KEY (org-level) and REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY (project override). 2) rotate project key via console -> key replaced. 3) clients do a quick fetch and start new streams. Some streams still pick up the old key and get 401 until the process restarts or the cache TTL expires.

liz: Do we have a TTL on the credential cache? I thought we used short TTL + event hook from the control plane to invalidate.

maya: TTL is 60s by default but our long-lived streaming code holds a pointer to the cached token and never rebinds it per-request. So even after the cache entry updates, the streamer keeps using its local ref.

ash: Oof. That matches a bug I fixed in the CLI last year: interactive sessions rebind on every reconnect. But the SDK streaming client is different.

maya: Also found confusion in env var precedence — sampleapp doc says project var should be REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY but SDK expects REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT for programmatic overrides. So onboarding docs + SDK parity mismatch. New users rotate the wrong key thinking they've scoped it.

sam: Noted. Two immediate items: (1) implement rebind-on-rotate for streaming client; (2) document exact env var names in sampleapp and unify names across SDKs.

liz: For (1) maybe expose a small listener API: credentials.onChange(callback) so streaming client can swap header atomically. That avoids polling TTL issues.

maya: I can prototype a tiny patch that emits an event from the credential manager when keys rotate (server-driven or local rotate). POC:

```js
// in creds manager
const creds = new CredsStore();
// when rotation happens (console webhook or CLI rotate)
creds.update(newKey);
creds.emit('change');

// streaming client
creds.on('change', () => stream.setAuth(creds.current()));
```

sam: Love it. Make sure the API works with both ephemeral and KMS-backed creds. Also add a small integration test that simulates rotation during an open stream.

ash: For the env var parity, proposal: deprecate REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROJECT and use REDWOOD_PROJECT_KEY everywhere (SDKs + docs) with a compatibility shim that reads both for a year. Migration note in sampleapp README and a CLI warning when both present.

maya: Sounds good. One more gotcha — metrics and billing attribution flip during the 401 window because requests fall back to org key in some routing cases. That can skew cost attribution for customers. We should add a signal in the control plane logs when a stream returns 401 due to stale project key vs outright invalid token.

devex-bot: Reminder: file a spec in /docs/sdk-auth/ with migration plan and link the integration test. Tagging @eng-platform for runtime impact.

sam: I'll open the PR for the event API + streaming client changes. Maya, can you add the sampleapp doc fixes and a repro test? I'll draft the deprecation timeline for env vars.

maya: Yes — will push a small repro and the docs patch today. Starting with a minimal integration test that rotates keys and asserts no 401s during the window.

liz: Assigning follow-ups: sam -> PR for creds.onChange + unit tests; maya -> sampleapp doc + repro test; ash -> audit routing logic to ensure attribution isn't silently switching to org key.

ash: On it. I'll also check Dedicated/Private builds for any difference in key webhook paths (KMS vs local HSM).

maya: Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
